name: Tallgrass Prairie National Preserve
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Tallgrass Prairie National Preserve in the Flint Hills of east-central Kansas protects a remnant of the tallgrass prairie ecosystem that once covered 170 million acres of North America — from Indiana to Kansas and from Canada to Texas. Less than 4 percent of the original tallgrass prairie remains today, making it one of the most endangered ecosystems on the continent, and the Flint Hills contain the largest remaining expanse. The preserve was established in 1996 through a public-private partnership between the National Park Service and The Nature Conservancy. The nearly 11,000-acre site includes the historic Spring Hill/Z Bar Ranch with an 1881 limestone ranch house, a massive stone barn, and a one-room schoolhouse. A bison herd was reintroduced to the preserve in 2009.
